children.text: ity āruhya parāṃ koṭiṃ krodho raudrātmatāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus anger, having mounted to its highest limit, has assumed the nature of the furious sentiment;

children.text: bhīmasya paśyataḥ śatrum ity etad rasavadvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this speech of <s>Bhīma</s>, as he sees his enemy, is rasavat.

children.text: ajitvā sārṇavām urvīm aniṣṭvā vividhair makhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Without conquering the earth with its oceans, without sacrificing with various rites,

children.text: adatvā cārtham arthibhyo bhaveyaḥ pārthivaḥ katham ||

is capable of establishing the rasavat quality of these utterances.

corpse-eaters, adorned with entrails, dance together with headless trunks.

children.text: śākhāś ca mandirāṇy eṣāṃ citraṃ nandanaśākhinām ||

children.text: iha tv aṣṭarasāyattā rasavattā smṛtā girām ||
children.translated_text: but here the rasavat quality of utterances is remembered as dependent on the eight rasas.

children.text: apakartāham asmīti hṛdi te mā sma bhūd bhayam
children.translated_text: "Do not let there be fear in your heart that I am one who does harm.

children.text: vimukheṣu na me khaḍgaḥ prahartuṃ jātu vāñchati ||
children.translated_text: My sword never desires to strike those whose faces are turned away."

children.text: iti muktaḥ paro yuddhe niruddho darpaśalinā
children.translated_text: Thus, when an enemy restrained in battle is released by some man full of pride,

children.text: artham iṣṭam anākhyāya sākṣāt tasyaiva siddhaye
children.translated_text: When, without directly stating the intended meaning, for the very accomplishment of that meaning,

"That cuckoo is biting the mango-blossom cluster;

children.text: tam ahaṃ vārayiṣyāmi yuvābhyāṃ svairam āsyatām ||
children.translated_text: I shall drive it away. You two may sit at ease."

some woman, wishing their festival of love there to be completed, withdrew from that place.
When someone has begun some undertaking and then, by the power of fate,
the acquisition of the means to accomplish it occurs, they call that samāhita (fortunate coincidence).

children.text: mānam asyā nirākartuṃ pādayor me patiṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: "To remove her sulking pride, I was going to fall at her feet;
fortunately this risen thundercloud's roar has occurred to help me."

children.text: āśayasya vibhūter vā yan mahatvam anuttamam
children.translated_text: That unsurpassed greatness of intention or of prosperity

children.text: udāttaṃ nāma taṃ prāhur alaṃkāraṃ manīṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise call the ornament named udātta (elevated grandeur).

children.text: guroḥ śasanam atyetuṃ na śaśāka sa rāghavaḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Rāghava</s> could not transgress his teacher's command,
though he was unshaken even under the burden of the task of cutting off <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s heads.
Surrounded by hundreds of reflections cast upon walls of jewels,
the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> was recognized with difficulty in truth by <s>Āñjaneya</s>.
In the former case the greatness of intention, and here the weight of prosperity,

children.text: suvyañjitam iti proktaṃ udāttadvayam apy adaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been well suggested; thus both kinds of udātta have been stated.
Apahnuti (denial) is, after denying something, the showing of another meaning:

children.text: na pañceṣu smaras tasya sahasraṃ patriṇām iti ||
children.translated_text: "He does not have five arrows; <s>Smara</s> has a thousand feathered arrows."

children.text: candanaṃ candrikā mando gandhavāhaś ca dakṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Sandalwood, moonlight, and the gentle southern fragrance-bearing wind:

children.text: seyam agnimayī sṛṣṭir mayi śītā parān prati ||
children.translated_text: this creation is made of fire for me, though cool toward others.

Speech that is desired as śliṣṭa (punning), having many meanings while connected with one form,
is of two kinds: with undivided words and mostly with divided words.
That radiant one, with a red disk, has risen upward;

children.text: rājā harati lokasya hṛdayaṃ mṛdubhiḥ karaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king takes the heart of the world with gentle rays, or hands.
Joining with the maker of night, moving on the path of the constellations,

children.text: rājñā pradoṣo mām ittham apriyaṃ kiṃ na bādhate ||
children.translated_text: why should evening, with the king, not torment me in this unpleasant way?
Puns whose scope is simile, metaphor, objection, contrast, and the like

children.text: prāg eva darśitāḥ śleṣā darśyante ke canāpare ||
children.translated_text: have already been shown; now some others are shown.
There is one with an identical action, another with a non-contradictory action,

children.text: viruddhakarmā cāsty anyaḥ śleṣo niyamavān api ||
children.translated_text: another with contradictory objects, and also a rule-bound pun.

Curved, naturally sweet, and expressing intense passion,

children.text: dṛśo dūtyaś ca karṣanti kāntābhiḥ preṣitāḥ priyān ||
children.translated_text: the glances, like female messengers, sent by beloved women draw their lovers.

This one, displaying passion intensified by the union with wine,
the ray of <s>dharma</s> disappears, but the passion born from the body expands.

children.text: nistriṃśatvam asāv eva dhanuṣy evāsya vakratā
children.translated_text: That same sword-like harshness belongs only to the sword; the crookedness of this king belongs only to his bow,

children.text: śareṣv eva narendrasya mārgaṇatvaṃ ca vartate ||
children.translated_text: and the quality of being “seekers” belongs only to the king’s arrows.

children.text: padmānām eva daṇḍeṣu kaṇṭakas tvayi rakṣati
children.translated_text: When you protect the earth, thorns exist only on the stalks of lotuses;
or rather, they are seen also in the embraces of passionate couples.

children.text: dakṣaḥ prajāpatiś cāsīt svāmī śaktidharaś ca saḥ ||

though a god, he was not dull-witted; though <s>Śaṃkara</s>, he possessed no serpents.

children.text: na kaṭhoraṃ na vā tīkṣṇam āyudhaṃ puṣpadhanvanaḥ
children.translated_text: The weapon of the flower-bowed god is neither hard nor sharp;
nevertheless, by it the three worlds were completely conquered.

children.text: tathāpy eṣā tapobhaṅgaṃ vidhātuṃ vedhaso 'py alam ||

children.text: na baddhā bhrūkuṭir nāpi sphurito daśanacchadaḥ
children.translated_text: No frown was knit, nor did the lip tremble;

children.text: na ca raktābhavad dṛṣṭir jitaṃ ca dviṣatāṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: nor did the eye become red, and yet the whole race of enemies was conquered.

children.text: na rathā na ca mātaṅgā na hayā na ca pattayaḥ
children.translated_text: There are no chariots, no elephants, no horses, and no foot-soldiers;
by women’s sidelong glance alone the three worlds are conquered.

children.text: ekacakro ratho yantā vikalo viṣamā hayāḥ
children.translated_text: Its chariot has one wheel, its driver is disabled, and its horses are uneven;

children.text: ākrāmaty eva tejasvī tathāpy arko nabhastalam ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless the brilliant sun strides over the sky.

children.text: ayam eva kramo 'nyeṣāṃ bhedānām api kalpane ||
children.translated_text: This very procedure is to be applied in forming the other varieties as well.

children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>, and you too

children.text: api te rūpam asmākaṃ tanvi tāpāya kalpate ||

bring tears to the eyes of travelers, though they do not touch them.

for whom does your glance become trustworthy, sweet-speaking girl?
Thus this ornament is understood to be of many kinds.

with foods easily obtained without effort, such as grass, darbha, and sprouts.
Here this very life of deer, though not the real topic, is praised
by a proud man wearied in mind by the hardship of serving a king.

children.text: yadi nindann iva stauti vyājastutir asau smrtā
children.translated_text: If someone praises while seeming to blame, that is remembered as vyājastuti (disguised praise);

children.text: doṣābhāsā guṇā eva labhante hy atra saṃnidhim ||
children.translated_text: for here apparent faults come into proximity with virtues themselves.

children.text: tvayā rājñāpi saiveyaṃ jitā mā bhūn madas tava ||
children.translated_text: by you too, though a king, this same world has been conquered. Let there be no pride in you.

children.text: puṃsaḥ purāṇād ācchidya śrīs tvayā paribhujyate
children.translated_text: After tearing fortune away from the ancient man, you enjoy her;

children.text: rājann ikṣākuvaṃśasya kim idaṃ tava yujyate ||
children.translated_text: O king, how is this fitting for you, born in the lineage of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>?
Your wife, the earth, is joined to the enjoyment of serpents;

children.text: ahaṅkāraḥ parāṃ koṭim ārohati kutas tava ||
children.translated_text: how then does your arrogance climb to the highest limit?
Thus the varieties of vyājastuti, penetrated by śleṣa (double meaning),
and other such varieties, should be recognized; their extension is endless.
If, by turning to another matter, some result similar to that thing,

children.text: sad asad vā nidarśyeta yadi tat syān nidarśanam ||
children.translated_text: whether real or unreal, is shown, then that is nidarśana (illustrative indication).

children.text: udayann eṣa savitā padmeṣv arpayati śriyam
children.translated_text: This rising sun bestows beauty upon lotuses,
as if to make known that the fruit of prosperity is favoring one’s friends.
A mass of darkness, touched by moonbeams, goes to defeat at once,
indicating the miserable end of those who oppose a king.

children.text: arthānāṃ yo vinimayaḥ parivṛttis tu sā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and the exchange of objects is remembered as parivṛtti (exchange).

children.text: saha dīrghā mama śvāsair imāḥ samprati rātrayaḥ
children.translated_text: These nights now are long together with my sighs;

children.text: pāṇḍurāś ca mamaivāṅgeḥ saha tāś candrabhūṣaṇāh ||

children.text: patanti ca samaṃ teṣām asubhir malayānilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the Malaya winds fall upon them together with their life-breaths.
Spring days, beautiful with the calls of cuckoos and with fragrant forest winds,
increase together with people’s joys.

children.text: ity udāhṛtayo dattāḥ sahokter atra kāś cana ||
children.translated_text: Thus some examples of sahokti have been given here.

children.text: kriyate parivṛtteś ca kiṃ cid rūpanidarśanam ||

By your arm, giving sword-blows to kings,

children.text: śleṣaḥ sarvāsu puṣṇāti prāyo vakroktiṣu śriyam
children.translated_text: Śleṣa, for the most part, nourishes beauty in all vakroktis (crooked expressions);

children.text: bhinnaṃ dvidhā svabhāvoktir vakroktiś ceti vāṅmayam ||
children.translated_text: literature is divided in two: svabhāvokti (natural description) and vakrokti.

children.text: tad bhāvikam iti prāhuḥ prabandhaviṣayaṃ guṇam
children.translated_text: They call that bhāvika, a quality whose object is a prabandha (connected composition);

children.text: bhāvaḥ kaver abhiprāyaḥ kāvyeṣv āsiddhi saṃsthitaḥ ||

The mutual assistance of all the stages of the subject matter,
the non-performance of useless details, and description in the proper place,
the manifestation, by the force of the sequence of expression, even of a profound subject:

children.text: bhāvāyattām idaṃ sarvam iti tad bhāvikaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this depends upon bhāva; therefore they know it as bhāvika.
And whatever has been described in another treatise as the marks and so on of the limbs of juncture and the limbs of action,
that, here, we have intended precisely as an ornament.

children.text: panthāḥ sa eṣa vivṛtaḥ parimāṇavṛttyā saṃhṛtya vistaram anantam alaṅkriyāṇām
children.translated_text: This path of the ornaments has been opened up in a measured mode, after compressing their endless expanse;

children.text: vācām atītya viṣayaṃ parivartamānān abhyāsa eva vivarītum alaṃ viśeṣān ||
children.translated_text: as for the distinctions that move about beyond the range of words, only practice is sufficient to disclose them.

children.text: ity ācāryadaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau kāvyādarśe 'rthālaṅkāravibhāgo nāma dvitīyo paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, called the division of ornaments of meaning, in the <s>Kāvyādarśa</s>, the work of the teacher <s>Daṇḍin</s>.
